brief: A display stand with the large platform on a spike where three bases meet.

requirements.requirement: Three bases that meet at one point
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0, piece:0,-1,0 and piece:-1,0,0 (all full bases) touch each other, bolted together by 3 joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: A spike where the three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#-1,0|0,-1|0,0 is a mount spike at the corner shared by all three bases.

requirements.requirement: Large platform on the spike, as a display stand
requirements.evidence: The large platform (platform-lrg) is fitted to the spike and listed in the BOM as spike-acc-platform-lrg. No prop was placed on it because the configurator doesn't allow props on a spike platform.

finish.summary:
I built the display stand. Three full hex bases sit in a triangle: the one already there at (0,0) plus new ones at (0,-1) and (-1,0). A mount spike stands at the corner where all three meet, and the large platform is fitted to it. I then capped every open face (12 solid end caps) and bolted the joints between the bases (3 joint bolts). There are 17 printed parts, about 1,099 g of filament and roughly 1,608 minutes of printing. The final check passed with no rule errors, and the parts don't overlap each other.

I didn't add any display props. The configurator doesn't let props sit on a spike or its platform, and the bases have no covers to put things on. So the build shows the stand itself, with nothing displayed on it.

The BOM notes say to tighten the M6 bolts to about 2 N·m by hand only.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
